---
title: "Troubleshooting"
description: "Symptoms, causes and fixes"
toc: true
---

@tbl-troubleshooting collects the symptoms ArduinoDriver's own documentation
names, with causes and fixes; the sections below give the detail behind each
row.

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `no UsbIo device found` / device not found | the sketch is not running, or a permissions problem | check the sketch is uploaded and running; if `arduino-io list` shows it under "Not probed", complete [Linux](host-linux.qmd) or [Windows](host-windows.qmd) host setup |
| `cannot claim UsbIo interface ... LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS` | another process already has the board open, or the OS permission setup is missing | close other `arduino-io`/driver processes; install the udev rule (Linux) or bind WinUSB (Windows) |
| `bulk IN transfer failed: LIBUSB_ERROR_IO` while streaming | marginal USB High Speed link — seen on a Portenta H7 plugged straight into a Mac USB-C port | put a USB hub between the computer and the board (see [macOS host](host-macos.qmd)) |
| `info` succeeds but `flags` has no `streaming` | board's core cannot add a streaming endpoint (Renesas: UNO R4 Minima, Nano R4), or firmware predates streaming support | check [Supported boards](boards.qmd); if the board should support it, reflash the current `UsbIo` ([Flashing the firmware](firmware.qmd)) |
| `GET_INFO` answers with `n_pins == 0` | the sketch has enumerated but has not reached `UsbIo.begin()` yet | the driver already retries for up to 2 s; if it still fails, check for blocking code in `setup()` before `UsbIo.begin()` |
| a call throws `DeviceBusy` | a stream is running on this device | stop the stream first (`stream.stop()` / `stream$stop()`, or Ctrl-C on `arduino-io stream`) |
| upload cannot find the board | the board needs the bootloader | double-tap reset (mbed and SAMD boards), re-run `arduino-cli board list`, upload to the new port |
| achieved stream rate far below the requested rate | the sketch samples at most one record per `loop()`; the loop rate is the ceiling | remove `delay()` and slow code from `loop()` ([Flashing the firmware](firmware.qmd#adding-your-own-code)), or accept the rate the summary line reports |
| UNO R4 Minima / Nano R4 not usable from Windows | the Renesas core exposes no vendor interface for WinUSB to bind | use [Linux](host-linux.qmd) or [macOS](host-macos.qmd) with these boards, or pick a different board ([Supported boards](boards.qmd)) |

: Symptom, cause and fix. {#tbl-troubleshooting}

## Device not found

If `arduino-io list` shows nothing at all for the board, first confirm the
`UsbIo` sketch is actually running (a `Serial.print()` heartbeat, or the
board's own activity LED, helps here). If the board shows up under a
separate "Not probed" block instead of the main list, that is a permissions
problem, not a missing device — see [Linux host](host-linux.qmd) for the
udev rule or [Windows host](host-windows.qmd) for WinUSB.

## `cannot claim UsbIo interface ... LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS`

Two causes produce the same message: another program already has the board
open (only one process can use a board at a time — close any other
`arduino-io` invocation, including a leftover `stream`), or the host-level
permission setup from [Linux host](host-linux.qmd) or [Windows
host](host-windows.qmd) is missing or incomplete.

## `LIBUSB_ERROR_IO` on a streaming board

Seen specifically on the Portenta H7's USB High Speed link plugged straight
into some computer ports (documented on a Mac's USB-C port). See [macOS
host](host-macos.qmd) for the full symptom and the USB-hub fix; the fix
applies regardless of host OS if the same symptom shows up elsewhere.

## Board answers `info` but the `streaming` flag is missing

Two different situations look the same in `arduino-io info`'s output:

1. **The board cannot stream at all.** UNO R4 Minima and Nano R4 use the
   Renesas core, whose fixed USB descriptors cannot add the bulk endpoint
   streaming needs — `arduino-io info` never shows `streaming` for these two
   boards, on any firmware version.
2. **The firmware predates streaming support.** On a board that *should*
   support streaming (any mbed or SAMD board), a missing `streaming` flag
   means the sketch was built from an older `UsbIo` revision. Reflash the
   current firmware — see [Flashing the firmware](firmware.qmd).

Check [Supported boards](boards.qmd) to know which case applies to your
board before assuming it needs reflashing.

## `GET_INFO` with `n_pins == 0`

This means the sketch has enumerated on USB but has not yet reached
`UsbIo.begin()` in `setup()`. The driver already waits up to 2 seconds for
this and normally never surfaces it. If it persists, look for blocking code
(a `delay()`, a sensor that waits for a bus, a `while` loop) before
`UsbIo.begin()` in your sketch.

## `DeviceBusy` while a stream runs

While a stream is running, the `Device` refuses every other call —
`pin_mode()`, digital/analog/PWM/DAC I/O, `reset()` — with `DeviceBusy`. This
is not a fault: stop the stream first (`stream.stop()` in Python,
`stream$stop()` in R, or let the object go out of scope / use its context
manager), or let a running `arduino-io stream` finish or be interrupted with
Ctrl-C.

## Upload cannot find the board

Put the board in bootloader mode: double-tap the reset button on mbed boards
(Portenta, GIGA, Nano 33 BLE — the LED breathes) and on SAMD boards. The
board enumerates under a *different* port in bootloader mode, so re-run
`arduino-cli board list` and upload to the new port. See [Flashing the
firmware](firmware.qmd#bootloader-and-the-changing-port) for the full detail,
including that the port changes again after a successful upload.

## Achieved stream rate far below the requested rate

The firmware samples at most one record per `loop()` iteration, so the
achieved rate cannot exceed the sketch's loop rate — requesting more simply
gets you the loop rate instead, and the summary line reports what was
actually achieved. If your own code was added to the sketch (see [Adding
your own code](firmware.qmd#adding-your-own-code)), remove `delay()` calls
and slow operations from `loop()`; if the sketch is already the plain
`UsbIoDevice` example, the board's own loop speed is the ceiling, and only
the Portenta H7's has been measured (about 32 kHz on one channel, 23.5 kHz on
two, with the unmodified example sketch).

## Windows on Renesas boards

UNO R4 Minima and Nano R4 cannot be used with `arduino-io` on Windows at all
— not a missing driver, but no vendor interface on the device to bind one to.
See [Windows host](host-windows.qmd) for why, and use Linux or macOS with
these two boards instead.
